999.t: Louis Dumaine, how long with Kid Howard, and George Lewis
999.s: He identifies Louis Dumaine, says he played with Howard off and on, and talks about George Lewis.
999.q: That's the thing I was trying to call. That's the guy made an offer to me to teach me music. He was crazy about my bass drum playing too. That's the name I was trying to call, Louis Dumaine. Yeah. Fine old man. Fine, fine guy. He was playing in the same band with us when Howard had his brass band.

391.t: Bands heard: George Lewis at Preservation Hall
391.s: The most inspiring sets were George Lewis's quartet and his band with Kid Howard at Preservation Hall.
391.q: Uh, uh, yes, we've heard quite a few. I'd say we've heard about ten, in, not as many days. Uh, well, the most inspired, band we've heard, has been a quartet. Uh, George Lewis, Jim Robinson, Joe Watkins, and, uh, Dolly Adams. It was last, Friday night, I think, at Preservation Hall. Anyway, it…

259.t: Zeb Lenard, Buddy Petit and George Lewis's early bands
259.s: Vincent says Zeb worked with Buddy Petit and Jack, and that Petit left for Chicago. George Lewis worked with Vincent more than with any band and also with Petit and Kid Howard.
259.ch: Casa, Zeb Lenard and Little Joe
259.q: Who did Zeb work with? Zeb? Buddy Petit, yeah. Zeb? When I was here. Were you working with Jack when Jack was working with him? No. He used to work with Jack. He stayed with kids with her a long time. And he stayed with Buddy. Me and him was the guy that was Buddy, you see. But Peter, he had left…

264.t: Covington band members, George Washington and living across the lake
264.s: Looking at a c. 1921 photo, Zardis talks about the older band members, George Washington's earlier bands and death, and the band living in Covington as its base for work in nearby towns.
264.ch: Opening and the Buddy Petit band
264.q: Right around that time. How old were you then about, you don't look very old then. No I was a kid then. I was real. I don't think I was 20 years old and that's what I was telling you about. But Buddy was older than me. Yeah. Yeah. Buddy was way older than me. And first of all, well Fissel and Buddy…

628.t: Playing with George Lewis and the St. Bernard dances for Father Oswald
628.s: Williams recalls playing with George Lewis around 1945 and the band for Father Oswald's school dances in St. Bernard Parish, with Lawrence Marrero, Slow Drag, Paul Barnes and Eulie Young.
628.ch: George Lewis and the 1946 Jazz Foundation concert
628.q: No, no. I remember playing with him in between time because I got a book here. Paul Barnes was in the army. And I built this school. You might get some of it out of here.

1026.t: George Lewis away at the start, Sales as bandleader, and the quartets
1026.s: George left town as the hall began, declined to lead, and played as sideman; Sales became leader of the band, and the quartet with Jim and others is recalled.
1026.q: And, right when the hall started, George left town. And he never played at the hall, you know, when it was actually a hall. And he was, the first time he really started playing, he came back from a trip. Where'd he go in, 61? I think he went. To Europe? To the Dardy Tate. Yeah. Yeah. He came back.…

875.t: Mike Neal and first playing with George Lewis
875.s: Mike Neal lived with Howard; the 1940s recordings and early work with George Lewis before Bunk Johnson.
875.q: Mike Neal, bro, played with me. In fact he lived with me before I went overseas. I left him at the house when I lived on St. Philip Street. He was staying with me. And he played with me in the big band.

857.t: White Carnations records in Jacksonville and George Washington
857.s: Foster recalls recording with the White Carnations in Jacksonville, George Washington's part, Buddy Petit's band photo, and where George is now.
857.q: The White Carnations. Oh. Do you remember the label? No, I think it was uh... Oak Hill, I think. Oak Hill. Was it made here in town? No, it was Jacksonville, Florida.

632.t: Greenwood journal: taping the Lewis band and Lewis's age
632.s: Debate over who taped Lewis at Bourbon Street, Lawrence Marrero's heart and George Lewis's plan to quit; then Feb 1950 outings with Look staff.
632.q: Greenwood taped to well you know the impression I had and I may be wrong is that either Greenwood and Otto both taped the same night or that Greenwood dubbed Otto's tapes well the the two

829.t: Playing with Buddy Petit around the lake; George Lewis in Mandeville
829.s: Asked about early dance bands, Robertson says he played with Buddy Petit, who had a boat run on the lake, and recalls George Lewis playing with them in Mandeville.
829.q: Oh yeah, he had that boat. One of the best clients that we had here, he left here and went to California. His wife died over the river not so long ago. Not good to know, he come from Manneville too, but I didn't know that boy.

138.t: Manuel Perez, Barbarin and George Lewis bands
138.s: Russell and Laine discuss Manuel Perez's military band and Paul Barbarin and George Lewis bands playing music like Laine's.
138.q: He couldn't take it away from him. He was sort of a military band. He had a good band. Now there's only one band in this town that plays almost. Well, in fact, if you sit up, heard my band play and walk away and hear this colored band play, you'd hear my same stuff. What's his name? Paul Barbarian.…

392.t: Hiring George Lewis and hearing him first
392.s: Bands were rotated; Papa Celestin's last steady job was here. Sid first heard George Lewis on records and at the Patek Lounge, then hired him twice for months.
392.ch: George Lewis and the house bands
392.q: There were a number of good bands around town, of which George had one. And our policy was not to keep the same band for much too long. We would change bands and alternate bands. Paul Baldwin would work a while. By a while, I mean some months. George would come in with his band, and this actually…

161.t: Bunk Johnson at the Stuyvesant Casino and George Lewis
161.s: He saw Bunk Johnson's opening night, got to know George Lewis, and assesses the band's playing and Lewis's later meeting.
161.q: You could see me with my first wife, we were still going together. She’s sitting on my knee and we’re smiling listening to Bunk Johnson. It’s a marvelous thing. So I liked it, and I got to know George Lewis rather well. And he hated Bunk Johnson and the whole band hated Bunk. It was like — and…
